newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, looking well, sees NATO deal with Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, looking well, sees NATO deal with Clinton.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, looking thin but lively on his first public appearance for nearly two months, said on Sunday he expected to strike a deal on NATO expansion plans at next month's summit with Bill Clinton.

Yeltsin, who met U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Friday, told reporters Russia would stall the inclusion of former Soviet bloc states into the Atlantic alliance as long as possible. He said he hoped to reach a compromise when he met the U.S. president in Helsinki on March 20-21.

"We are firm in our position. We are opposed to NATO enlargement. Our task now is to stall it as long as possible and not allow the renewal of confrontation," Yeltsin said after laying a wreath to mark Defenders of the Fatherland Day.

"We have agreed to look for a compromise and I think we will find this compromise at the summit we are holding with President Clinton on March 20-21," he said at Moscow's war memorial outside the Kremlin Wall.

Yeltsin spent nearly 20 minutes on the ceremony and chatting with journalists, the first time he has been seen in public since he went down with pneumonia in early January, an illness which thwarted his attempt to make an early recovery from the heart bypass operation he underwent last November.

Walking a little stiffly but with confidence and speaking clearly, he told reporters he had lost 26 kg (57 pounds) during his illnesses of the past few months. "I have fully recovered now. I just have to gain some strength," he said, warning his opponents in parliament against attempts to unseat him.
